claim: Selecting a small relevant subset of a large fact library lifts prover success well above giving the prover everything; learned selectors beat rule-based ones (SInE, Sledgehammer MePo). Frozen-LLM agents show the same pattern with growing libraries (LEGO-Prover +3.3 points, Voyager 19 vs 26-36 iterations) and tool lists (RAG-MCP 43.1% vs 13.6%).
agent_test: Equal tokens: compare retrieving top-k subgoals/lemmas by learned score vs. rule filter vs. whole library in context.

claim: More premises is not better: prover success falls once the premise set passes a few hundred (Z3 12.4% at 256 vs 6.2% at 740; Vampire 18.1 vs 12.9; E parallel 20%+ at 512 to 15.6% at 2048). Also FormalML shows decline from M=10 to 20. For LLM readers the peak is lower and model-dependent: OP-RAG peak at 16K tokens (8B) and 32-48K (70B); Lost in the Middle gains flat past about 20 documents.
agent_test: Sweep k in {4,8,16,32,64} retrieved library items at fixed token budget; expect an inverted U.

claim: Unions of different selectors prove far more than any one: DeepMath union of all methods 80.9% vs best single 67.9% at largest cutoff; LeanPremise union with MePo 37.6 vs 33.3.
agent_test: Retrieve with two different retrievers (lexical + learned) and merge; compare to one retriever at equal total items.

claim: Selection quality is a bottleneck with measurable headroom: perfect premises give 50% vs 39% (Flyspeck), 43.0 vs 33.3 (LeanHammer), 56.2% ATP-provable vs 40% (Mizar).
agent_test: Oracle test: give the agent the ground-truth needed subgoals/lemmas and measure the gap vs. its own retrieval.

claim: Trained retrievers beat lexical baselines by a wide margin on Lean/Isabelle: Magnushammer 59.5 vs BM25 30.6 and Sledgehammer 38.3 (PISA); LeanDojo R@10 38.4 vs BM25 17.2.
agent_test: Compare BM25, general embedder and a task-tuned retriever over the agent's own subgoal library.

claim: General-purpose text embedders are weak on formal premise retrieval: ada-002 36.1 vs 59.5 trained (PISA); on LeanDojo random split embedders 25-27 R@10 vs 36.7 ReProver, but they beat ReProver on novel premises (23.8-24.7 vs 19.5).
agent_test: Test off-the-shelf embedder vs tuned scorer, split by seen vs unseen library items.

claim: Retrieval helps downstream proving, but modestly in the weaker setups: ReProver 51.2 vs 47.6 without retrieval (random); 26.3 vs 23.2 (novel_premises). Larger gains with a hammer coupling (Thor 39.0->57.0; +Magnushammer 71.0) and reasoning retrievers (LeanSearch v2 4->20% n=100).
agent_test: A/B the agent with and without library retrieval at equal tokens, split by old vs novel library items.

claim: Generalisation to unseen premises is the weak spot: ReProver pass@1 halves from 51.2 to 26.3 on novel_premises and R@10 38.4 to 27.6; GPT-4 29.0 to 7.4.
agent_test: Hold out a share of library items never seen in training/examples and measure retrieval and solve rate separately.

claim: A language model asked to name premises inside its own step rarely helps: steps with premises advance the proof 1.9% vs 28.2% for steps without; handing the premise choice to a dedicated tool (hammer) fixes it.
agent_test: Check how often agent-written subgoal references are valid vs. retrieved ones.

claim: Negative mining and hard negatives matter: DeepMath mining 61.3 to 66.4 (union over cutoffs); LeanDojo in-file negatives worth 2.7 R@1 and 5.3 R@10; LeanPremise loss mask and extraction worth 5-13 points recall@32.
agent_test: When ranking stored subgoals, include near-miss distractors in any scorer calibration.

claim: Pretraining/scaling helps but saturates: Magnushammer 0.1% of data with pretraining 39.2 vs 16.8 without; at full data 56.3 vs 53.0; LeanPremise 23M to 82M recall@32 67.8 to 72.7.
agent_test: Not testable without training; note only.

claim: Structure (graphs, dependency context) gives small, noisy gains: HolStep names alone give 81.5% at zero graph steps vs 90.3% full; Lean GNN ablations move R@10 by about 1 point; CSLibPremiseBench structure reranker +0.0175 MRR over BM25 but not better than BM25+symbol. Rango: BM25 over proof states beat CodeBERT dense by 46%.
agent_test: Test whether simple symbol-overlap matching equals a heavier structure-aware retriever on our library.

claim: Offline metrics may not predict prover success: XGBoost looked better on similarity but worse on ATP success (0.31 vs 0.40 NMT); labels from ATP proofs vs human proofs differ; LeanPremise recall numbers differ from Yang 2023 by upper-bound definition.
agent_test: Always score retrieval by downstream solve rate, not by retrieval recall alone.

claim: Label noise limits benchmarks: only 48.2% of proxy-linked premises appear in elaborated terms (CSLib); human-only labels give 54.0 vs augmented 56.3.
agent_test: Audit which stored items the agent truly used before treating them as ground truth.

claim: Reasoning-style retrieval (LLM rewrites query, sketches, judges candidates) beats fixed-embedding retrieval on informal-to-formal queries: group recall@10 46.1 vs 38.0 vs 9.3. Outside formal maths, BRIGHT shows the same: BM25 14.5 to 27.0 nDCG@10 with GPT-4 reasoning-step queries. The extra reasoning tokens are not charged to any budget in these papers.
agent_test: Compare plain embedding lookup with query rewriting before lookup at matched token cost; count rewrite tokens.

claim: Decomposing the goal then retrieving dependencies improves formalisation: DRIFT ConNF BEq+@1 54.84 full vs 4.47 without retrieval, 46.72 without decomposition.
agent_test: Ablate decompose-then-retrieve vs retrieve-on-whole-goal.

claim: Retrieval gains in downstream provers are small for strong whole-proof models: Lean Finder gives +0.4 miniF2F for Goedel-Prover-SFT and +2.2 ProofNet DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5-RL pass@1.
agent_test: Check whether a strong base agent needs retrieval at all on easy items.

claim: Iterating selection and proving in rounds keeps adding gains: MizAR rounds raised re-proved Mizar from 48% to 55.6% (6 rounds); RL without human proofs reaches over 90% of human-RL performance (56.3 vs 59.9).
agent_test: Iterate: add solved items back to the library and re-measure.

claim: Easy filters limit the problem: iProver already solves 86% of one subset with no selection, so selection gains there are bounded; random forest matches k-NN Cover at 20x speed.
agent_test: Check problems where no retrieval already succeeds; do not count them as retrieval wins.

claim: For a frozen LLM, reading the full context beats chunk retrieval on accuracy when it fits, but retrieval needs 38-61% of the tokens in Self-Route and a retrieve-first-then-fall-back router keeps most of the accuracy (Gemini 46.41 vs LC 49.70; GPT-4o 48.89 vs 48.67). Studies conflict on the winner (OP-RAG: 16K retrieved tokens beat 117K full context, F1 44.43 vs 34.26), depending on whether needed facts are scattered.
agent_test: Two-step lookup: top-5 items first, widen to the full library only when the agent says it cannot answer; compare tokens and solve rate to full-library-in-context.

claim: Tool and skill lists show a crossover: putting all items in the prompt collapses past roughly 30 to 100 items (RAG-MCP 13.62% vs 43.13% with retrieval; success above 90% under 30 candidates), while Voyager's top-5 retrieval from a growing library has 96.5% recall at 5.
agent_test: Sweep library size 10, 30, 100, 300 with and without retrieval; record the size where the no-retrieval arm falls behind.

claim: Near-miss (high-similarity, unhelpful) items harm LLM readers much more than random ones: one hard distractor cost up to 25% accuracy and many cost up to 67% (Llama2, NQ), stronger retrievers give harder negatives, and a stronger retriever can lower end accuracy at large k.
agent_test: Add k near-miss items to a prompt and measure the drop; add an entailment filter and measure harm vs lost recall.

claim: Position and amount of retrieved items matter for LLM readers: gold-in-the-middle drops accuracy over 20% and at 20-30 documents the worst case is below closed-book; reader accuracy saturates long before retriever recall.
agent_test: Place the best match first or last in the prompt; do not exceed about 10-20 items without testing.

claim: Growing a library during the run helps a frozen LLM, and the gain widens as the library fills: LEGO-Prover 50.4% vs 47.1% without library at 50 attempts (miniF2F-valid); Voyager without library plateaus. Rango shows retrieval of earlier proofs substitutes for project knowledge in weights (gain from having project files in the weights: 15% and 11% with proof retrieval vs 26% and 43% without).
agent_test: Run with an initially empty library and track solve rate vs number of stored items; compare against a frozen pre-filled library.

claim: Retrieval keyed on the current goal and returning earlier solved goals with their solutions beats lemma-only retrieval, and lexical match beats dense embeddings for proof states: Rango proof retriever +47%, lemma retriever +3%, BM25 +46% over CodeBERT. A plain-language gloss on the stored state roughly triples recall@1 (Lean Finder 24.6 vs 8.3).
agent_test: Store (goal text, short gloss, solution) per subgoal; retrieve with BM25 over goal plus gloss; compare against embeddings.

claim: The oracle gap in non-formal QA exists but is only partly closed by retrieval: BRIGHT StackExchange QA with Claude-3.5-Sonnet gives no retrieval 77.7, best retriever 79.6, oracle documents 81.8 (46% of the gap); Lost in the Middle gives closed-book 56.1 vs oracle 88.3 for GPT-3.5.
agent_test: Measure agent solve rate with ground-truth needed subgoals injected vs own retrieval.

claim: Training or calibrating a selector on near misses needs positive-aware negatives: negatives that score above about 95% of the positive hurt; NV-Retriever average NDCG@10 0.5856 (TopK-PercPos) vs 0.5407 naive top-k vs 0.5248 random.
agent_test: When building contrast examples from the library, skip the top-ranked items for a different model and keep those scoring under 95% of the true match.
